changes.motivation: The custom sysz script was significantly slower to start than the original because `_sysz_sort` spawned a subshell + `printf | sed` pipeline for every unit to strip ANSI escape codes. With 300–500+ units on a typical NixOS system, this caused 600–1000+ fork/exec calls on every startup and on every ctrl-r/ctrl-s reload.
changes.summary: Replaced the `printf '%s' "$unit_colored" | sed ...` subprocess call in `_sysz_sort` with inline bash parameter expansion (`${unit_colored//$'\e'[\[(]*([0-9;])[@-n]/}`), matching the pattern already used by the existing `_strip_ansi` helper. This eliminates all subprocess spawning in the sort path.

problems: The script already had a `_strip_ansi` bash-native helper function but `_sysz_sort` duplicated the same logic using an external `sed` subprocess instead of calling or reusing the pattern. This inconsistency was the direct cause of the performance regression and was not documented anywhere — a future developer customizing the sort function would not know to avoid subprocess calls here.
